Two remedies were considered beyond the status quo: a diagnostic-only third orphan class, and a boundary refusal. The orphan class alone does not prevent malformed-terminal acceptance, because the fold would still fabricate the event; the refusal does. This bundle therefore exposes the `xml.parse` state on `LooseEvent` (so a consumer can refuse without turning `listLooseEvents` into a hard error) and refuses at **both** production write entry paths — ordinary `foldEpochImpl` and the supersede `discardAndFoldEpochImpl` — through one shared local helper, before any `discarded`, auto-open, or ledger write.
